newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-NAPOLI GET STADIUM BAN FOR CUP VIOLENCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NAPOLI GET STADIUM BAN FOR CUP VIOLENCE.

text.p: Napoli were banned on Wednesday from using their San Paolo stadium for their opening Italian Cup match of next season after crowd violence marred this year's final against eventual winners Vicenza.
Italy's serie A sporting judge also fined Napoli five million lire ($3,000) and Vicenza 25 million ($15,000).

Napoli striker Nicola Caccia was given a three-match ban and a two million lire fine ($1,200) for elbowing an opponent and insulting the referee during the May 29 second leg of the final in Vicenza, who won their first trophy in 95 years.

A contingent of Napoli fans who travelled from the southern port to the northern town threw flares at Vicenza supporters throughout the match and helmeted riot police eventually baton-charged them after the whistle.
The sporting judge said the behaviour of the Napoli fans had been "extraordinarily dangerous" and they had deliberately intended to hit spectators.
Vicenza fans were slammed for racist chants.
